chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah Al-Madainy from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic
So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord

He (peace be upon him) said: The man does something from the rewardable deeds, not seeking the Face of Allah by it, but rather seeking the approval (purification) of the people, desiring that the people hear of it (him). So this is the one who has associated (committed Shirk) with the worship of his Lord.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: There is no servant who conceals good, so the days pass forever until Allah manifests goodness for him, and there is no servant who conceals evil, so the days pass forever until Allah manifests the evil for him.

key_terms.تَزْكِيَةَ النَّاسِ: Seeking the approval or reputation among people
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (seeking His pleasure)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Shirk in worship according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expands the concept of Shirk in worship (18:110) to include 'hidden Shirk' (Shirk al-Khafi), where the intent is to gain human praise rather than divine pleasure. It further establishes the principle of divine manifestation, asserting that concealed righteous acts will eventually be revealed as good, while hidden sins will be exposed as evil, reinforcing the importance of sincerity (Ikhlas) in both public and private spheres.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[18:110] therefore whoever hopes to meet his Lord, so he should do righteous deeds, and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man does something from the Reward-able deeds, not seeking the Face of the Allah<sup>azwj</sup> by it, but rather for purifying the people desiring that the people would hear him with it (become famous). So this is the one who is associating (committing Shirk) with the worship of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a servant who does good deeds secretly, so the days go by for ever until Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Manifest goodness for him, and there is none from a servant who does an evil deed secretly, so the days would go by forever until Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Manifest the evil for him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mada’ini who has said the following:
“About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘. . .
whoever desires to meet his Lord should strive righteously and should worship no one besides Him,’ [18:110]

abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, “A man performs a good deed and thereby he does not seek rewards from Allah but rather he wants to purify people desiring them to hear him. He has made his obedience for Allah to be shared with others.”

The Imam then said, ‘Any servant (of Allah) who performs a good deed privately and times pass forever still, Allah will manifest its good (result) for him. Any servant (of Allah) who performs an evil deed privately and times pass forever still, Allah will uncover for him an evil (result).”’
